paragraphs: This paper studies how to make text-to-image diffusion models better reflect preferences. Earlier approaches treat the entire image-generation trajectory as receiving one overall reward. The authors argue that this treatment overlooks the sequence of decisions involved in generation and may reduce the effectiveness and efficiency of preference alignment.

Their alternative considers rewards at a finer temporal level and derives a practical training objective that places greater emphasis on the initial steps of reverse diffusion. They introduce temporal discounting into objectives resembling Direct Preference Optimization, while retaining the ability to train without an explicit reward model. This changes how different generation steps contribute to the alignment objective.

Experiments involving both individual prompts and multiple prompts show results competitive with strong relevant baselines in quantitative assessments and qualitative comparisons. The stated finding is competitiveness, rather than consistent superiority. The contribution is a way to account for the generation process’s temporal structure when learning from preferences, supported by further investigations into the approach.
icml-2024-a-dense-reward-view-on-alignin.tldr: A temporally discounted preference objective emphasizes early diffusion steps and achieves competitive text-to-image alignment results.

paragraphs: Predicting a crystal’s material properties involves more than estimating a single number. Properties such as dielectric, piezoelectric, and elastic responses are represented by tensors, whose components must behave consistently with the material’s symmetries. This paper addresses the challenge of predicting these properties while respecting both O(3) transformations and crystal space-group symmetries.

The authors introduce the General Materials Tensor Network, or GMTNet, with an architecture designed to satisfy these symmetry requirements. The central idea is to make the relevant transformation rules part of the prediction method itself. This matters because a tensor prediction must represent the same underlying material response consistently when the crystal is transformed in ways governed by those symmetries.

The work also provides a curated dataset and evaluation measures tailored to crystal tensors. Experiments report promising prediction performance across tensors of different orders, together with full consistency with intrinsic crystal symmetries. These findings support the combination of predictive modeling and explicit symmetry requirements for this family of material properties.
icml-2024-a-space-group-symmetry-informe.tldr: GMTNet predicts crystal tensor properties using an architecture designed to preserve the required spatial and crystal symmetries.

paragraphs: Federated learning involves clients whose data can differ substantially, making the choice of collaborators important. This paper asks whether a client should always cooperate with the clients most similar to itself. Its starting observation is that complementary data can provide useful information that very similar collaborators may not contribute.

The theoretical and empirical analyses suggest a more specific balance: encourage differences in the distribution of features while limiting differences in how those features relate to prediction targets. This distinguishes potentially useful diversity from disagreement about what the features mean for the task. The proposed FedSaC framework approximates a suitable cooperation network for each client by optimizing a weighted combination of model similarity and feature complementarity.

Experiments across unimodal and multimodal settings report substantial improvements over other state-of-the-art federated learning methods. The findings support cooperation that considers both shared predictive relationships and additional information. FedSaC is presented as adaptable to different degrees of data heterogeneity, rather than as a rule that the most similar or most different partner is always best.
icml-2024-balancing-similarity-and-compl.tldr: FedSaC improves federated cooperation by balancing model similarity with complementary feature distributions.

paragraphs: This paper examines how to choose between adding more layers to a neural network and making a network with relatively few layers wider. It compares these architecture families through their optimal generalization error under Sobolev losses. The purpose is to connect architectural choices to the mathematical learning problem instead of treating depth or width as universally preferable.

The analysis identifies several factors that influence the comparison: the number of available sample points, the number of network parameters, and the regularity associated with the loss function. More parameters tend to favor the wider networks considered in the study. More sample points and greater loss regularity instead tend to favor deeper networks.

These are directional conclusions within the paper’s analytical setting, so the relevant resources and loss properties must be considered together. The authors apply the theory to neural approaches for partial differential equations, including deep Ritz and physics-informed neural network methods. This gives the comparison a concrete role in guiding architecture design for those applications.
icml-2024-deeper-or-wider-a-perspective-.tldr: A theoretical comparison links the benefits of depth and width to sample count, parameter count, and Sobolev-loss regularity.

paragraphs: Efficient Transformer architectures aim to reduce computation, but their ability to replace standard Transformers also depends on the tasks they must solve. This paper investigates Sparse Transformers and Linear Transformers through reasoning tasks expressed as dynamic programming problems. Chain-of-thought prompting provides the setting for studying how these models carry out such computations.

The theoretical results show that both architectures are expressive enough to solve general dynamic programming tasks. However, their required model size grows with the size of the problem. This means that being able to represent a solution does not by itself establish a computational saving: the architecture may need to become larger as the reasoning task expands.

The authors also identify a class of dynamic programming problems for which these models can be more efficient than a standard Transformer. Experiments on representative tasks support the theoretical results. The paper therefore provides a task-dependent account of efficiency, explaining both a scaling requirement and circumstances in which the alternative architectures retain an advantage.
icml-2024-do-efficient-transformers-real.tldr: Sparse and Linear Transformers can solve general dynamic programming tasks, but their efficiency depends on task structure and required model growth.

paragraphs: DoraemonGPT is an LLM-driven system for understanding scenes that change over time, demonstrated as a video agent. Given a video and a question or task, it first converts relevant video information into a symbolic memory. This structured representation stores attributes that can support reasoning about both spatial relationships and temporal changes.

Specialized tools query that memory and return concise intermediate results. Additional plug-and-play tools provide access to external knowledge when a task requires expertise beyond the language model’s internal knowledge. The system therefore combines information extracted from the video with tools that help interpret what that information means for a particular task.

An LLM-driven planner uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to explore possible sequences of tool use. It feeds rewards from results back through the search to find feasible solutions, and can combine multiple solutions into an improved final answer. Evaluation covers three benchmarks and several in-the-wild scenarios. The contribution is an integrated approach to video representation, knowledge access, and tool planning for dynamic-scene understanding.
icml-2024-doraemongpt-toward-understandi.tldr: DoraemonGPT combines structured video memory, external tools, and tree-search planning to answer questions about dynamic scenes.

paragraphs: This paper distinguishes information represented inside a language model from its ability to express information as words. It calls the quantity and quality of information in neuron output vectors cognitive capability, and calls word-level output ability expressive capability. These are operational definitions used to study Baichuan-7B and Baichuan-33B through linear representations.

The analysis follows pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning from human feedback. In the studied models, cognitive capability is largely established during pretraining, while expressive capability develops predominantly during the later stages. Statistical analyses find a significant correlation between the two, suggesting that internal informational capacity may constrain what the model can express.

The paper also examines theoretical explanations for these different developmental patterns and their relationship to model architecture. It evaluates strategies such as few-shot learning and repeated sampling that can help bridge the gap without further optimization. The findings connect hidden representations to observable outputs, offering a way to interpret how different training stages affect what these models represent and communicate.
icml-2024-exploring-the-llm-journey-from.tldr: A study of Baichuan models finds that internal information develops mainly during pretraining, while expression improves chiefly during later alignment stages.

paragraphs: Models used in societal applications are often kept confidential for legal or privacy reasons. That confidentiality can make it difficult for people affected by predictions to assess claims about fairness. FairProof addresses this tension by providing a system for public verification of model fairness while preserving the model’s confidentiality.

The system uses zero-knowledge proofs as its cryptographic foundation. These support verification without requiring disclosure of the confidential model. The authors also develop a fairness certification algorithm specifically for fully connected neural networks, designing it to fit the requirements of the proof system. The contribution therefore connects the fairness certification procedure with the mechanism used to verify it publicly.

The authors implement FairProof in Gnark and report empirical evidence that the system is practically feasible. The stated scope of the certification algorithm is fully connected neural networks. Within that scope, the work demonstrates an approach to making fairness claims checkable while retaining confidentiality, addressing a concrete obstacle to scrutiny of models whose details cannot be released.
icml-2024-fairproof-confidential-and-cer.tldr: FairProof uses zero-knowledge proofs to publicly verify fairness certifications for confidential fully connected neural networks.

paragraphs: A pretrained model may encounter different data when deployed in a new environment. Adapting it can be difficult when only a few labeled examples from that environment are available. MixPro addresses this setting by combining the information in a large source dataset with the limited information provided by the target examples.

The method linearly mixes pretrained embeddings from the two datasets, creating a relatively large collection of mixed representations. These combinations preserve important features of both distributions while reducing the influence of noise specific to the small target sample. MixPro then trains a linear classifier on those representations, providing a lightweight way to adapt without fitting too closely to the few target examples.

The authors provide theoretical support for advantages over previous methods and evaluate MixPro across several model architectures and eight datasets with different distribution shifts. They report improvements over baselines of up to 7% using only two to four target examples. This is a reported maximum improvement, supporting the usefulness of representation mixing when target labels are scarce.
icml-2024-few-shot-adaptation-to-distrib.tldr: MixPro adapts pretrained models from very few target examples by mixing source and target embeddings before training a linear classifier.

paragraphs: Determining the direction of a causal relationship becomes harder when intervention data are limited and noisy. This paper moves beyond an idealized setting where interventions reveal edge directions with unlimited samples. It studies a setting in which repeated interventions on a node may be needed before the direction of a connection can be established.

The framework assumes causal sufficiency and access to the graph skeleton: the connections are available, while their directions remain to be determined. The authors formulate discovery as a structured multiple-testing problem. Their tests remain valid as evidence accumulates, and the framework can combine structured test statistics while using Meek rules to propagate conclusions about edge directions.

The method also accommodates robust testing, and simulations support its usefulness. The authors further connect graph verification to multi-constraint bandits and develop an algorithm for efficiently checking graph structure. The contribution is a statistical framework that treats uncertainty from finite data as part of causal discovery while exploiting relationships among the decisions being tested.
icml-2024-foundations-of-testing-for-fin.tldr: An anytime-valid testing framework uses finite intervention data to orient causal edges under causal sufficiency and a known graph skeleton.

paragraphs: Conditional diffusion methods can guide generation with a differentiable loss without additional training. However, that guidance can reduce sample quality and require small steps, slowing generation. This paper attributes the problem to guided samples departing from the intermediate data manifold, the structure they should follow during the sampling process.

The authors establish a lower bound on guidance-estimation error to theoretically demonstrate this deviation. They then propose Diffusion with Spherical Gaussian constraint, or DSG, inspired by how high-dimensional Gaussian distributions concentrate. Its constrained optimization keeps guidance within the intermediate manifold and permits larger guidance steps. A closed-form denoising solution makes the constraint practical to apply.

DSG can be added to existing training-free conditional diffusion methods with a small code change and almost no extra computational overhead. Experiments across several conditional generation tasks report improvements in both sample quality and time efficiency. The result connects a mathematical diagnosis of guidance error with a lightweight modification intended to make each guided sampling step more useful.
icml-2024-guidance-with-spherical-gaussi.tldr: DSG constrains diffusion guidance to an intermediate data manifold, enabling larger steps and improving sample quality and sampling efficiency.

paragraphs: This paper studies online linear quadratic regulator control with bandit feedback and semi-adversarial disturbances. Its focus is cost functions whose curvature varies. Earlier analyses require a uniform lower bound on strong convexity, which can be difficult to satisfy and can prevent algorithms from taking advantage of the curvature actually present.

The authors reduce the control problem to bandit convex optimization with memory. Their reduction retains history to avoid truncation errors that would otherwise be difficult to control. They then analyze a stability term affecting both regret and memory using the Newton decrement, a quantity drawn from interior-point optimization methods.

This analysis bounds the memory-related contributions introduced by the reduction and simplifies the treatment of heterogeneous curvature in bandit convex optimization. The resulting guarantees interpolate across different cost conditions: they recover existing bounds for convex and quadratic costs and give new implications when quadraticity is corrupted or decays. The contribution is an adaptive theoretical treatment of varying curvature within the stated control setting.
icml-2024-handling-heterogeneous-curvatu.tldr: A history-preserving reduction and new stability analysis yield bandit LQR guarantees that adapt to heterogeneous cost curvature.

paragraphs: Equivariant neural networks normally require the relevant symmetry group to be known in advance. Automatic symmetry discovery aims to learn that structure from data, but methods restricted to simple linear transformations cannot capture all the nonlinear symmetries of complex systems. This paper proposes Latent LieGAN, or LaLiGAN, to address that restriction.

LaLiGAN learns a mapping into a latent representation where the symmetries become linear. At the same time, it discovers the symmetries operating in that representation. Moving both tasks into one model allows a nonlinear transformation in the original data space to be represented through simpler structure in the learned space.

The authors prove that the model can express nonlinear symmetries under conditions on the group action; the result is therefore conditional. Experiments show accurate discovery of intrinsic symmetry in high-dimensional dynamical systems. The resulting latent representations also support equation discovery and long-term forecasting, suggesting that the learned organization is useful beyond identifying the symmetries themselves.
icml-2024-latent-space-symmetry-discover.tldr: LaLiGAN discovers nonlinear symmetries by jointly learning a latent space where those symmetries become linear.

paragraphs: Neural controllers can perform well empirically, but establishing formal stability for nonlinear systems remains challenging. This paper learns controllers together with Lyapunov certificates, which support stability guarantees over a region of attraction. Its training procedure combines fast empirical searches for violations with regularization designed to help obtain certifiable solutions.

The proposed formulation defines a larger verifiable region of attraction than previously shown in the literature. It also revises restrictive conditions on Lyapunov derivatives so that they focus on regions where certification is relevant. After training, branch-and-bound verification with linear bound propagation rigorously checks the Lyapunov condition, separating empirical learning from the formal verification step.

The full procedure is accelerated on GPUs and avoids the expensive SOS, MIP, and SMT solvers used by many existing approaches. The authors demonstrate formally stable output-feedback control using both learned neural controllers and learned neural observers. The guarantees concern the certified region of attraction, and the contribution expands the settings in which neural control can receive such guarantees.
icml-2024-lyapunov-stable-neural-control.tldr: A joint learning and verification framework provides Lyapunov stability certificates for neural controllers, including controllers with neural observers.

paragraphs: This paper studies how neural actor-critic reinforcement learning can learn useful features while moving toward an optimal policy. It considers overparameterized networks in a mean-field regime. The actor improves the policy through policy gradients, while the critic evaluates it through temporal-difference learning, so both parts contribute to the learning process.

For the critic, the authors introduce mean-field Langevin temporal-difference learning, combining Langevin dynamics with proximal temporal-difference updates. For the actor, they introduce mean-field Langevin policy gradients, using Wasserstein gradient flows to support exploration of parameter space. These methods are designed to study learning beyond the conventional lazy-training setting.

The analysis shows that the critic method identifies the true value function and that the actor sequence converges linearly to a globally optimal policy within a Kullback-Leibler divergence regularized framework. Particle and discretized analyses support the actor-critic convergence guarantees, alongside numerical analysis of the critic method. The global-optimality claim belongs to this specified framework, where feature learning is part of the theoretical treatment.
icml-2024-mean-field-langevin-actor-crit.tldr: Mean-field Langevin actor-critic methods obtain linear convergence guarantees toward global optimality in a KL-regularized framework beyond lazy training.

paragraphs: Coreset selection tries to identify a smaller training subset that retains much of the usefulness of the full dataset. This paper approaches the problem through the geometry of the model’s decision boundary. The central question is which examples are needed to reconstruct the boundary learned by a deep network trained on all the data.

The authors first develop a preliminary theoretical connection between data geometry and generalization. They then use those insights to select training samples for boundary reconstruction. This gives subset selection a concrete target: preserve the structure that the full-data model uses to separate predictions, rather than choosing examples without reference to that learned structure.

Experiments across popular benchmarks report improvements over multiple competing selection methods. On ImageNet-1K, the method removes half the training data while losing less than 1% accuracy. The authors also demonstrate and analyze transfer of the selected coresets across architectures. These results support the usefulness of boundary-oriented selection, including situations where the subset is used with a different network architecture.
icml-2024-mind-the-boundary-coreset-sele.tldr: Selecting examples to reconstruct a learned decision boundary removes half of ImageNet-1K training data with less than 1% accuracy loss.

paragraphs: Offline learning from observations aims to imitate an expert without collecting new interactions or observing the expert’s actions. The learner instead receives expert states and a separate collection of task-agnostic, non-expert state-action pairs. This paper studies how to make the learner’s state occupancy, describing the states it visits, match the expert’s.

Existing DICE methods use particular divergence measures or a dual formulation of Wasserstein distance that restricts the underlying distance metric. The proposed Primal Wasserstein DICE, or PW-DICE, directly minimizes the primal Wasserstein distance between learner and expert occupancies. It also uses a contrastively learned metric, providing greater flexibility in how differences between states are measured.

The theoretical framework generalizes SMODICE and unifies f-divergence and Wasserstein minimization. Empirical results show improvements over several state-of-the-art methods. The contribution links the choice of state-distance metric to the imitation objective, making that metric more adaptable within an offline setting where expert actions and additional environment interactions are unavailable.
icml-2024-offline-imitation-from-observa.tldr: PW-DICE improves offline imitation from expert states by matching state occupancies with primal Wasserstein distance and a learned metric.

paragraphs: Offline optimization seeks better solutions using a fixed dataset when evaluating the true objective is expensive. Many applications involve several objectives that conflict with one another, making improvement a matter of balancing competing goals. This paper addresses the comparatively limited development of offline multi-objective optimization by providing a benchmark for the setting.

The benchmark includes synthetic and real-world problems, datasets, and open-source examples to support comparisons between methods. The authors also examine how related approaches can be adapted through four components: the data, model architecture, learning algorithm, and search algorithm. This organizes the problem around the different decisions involved in building an offline optimization system.

Experiments show that offline multi-objective methods can improve on the best value in the training set. However, no particular method stands out significantly across the study. The benchmark therefore establishes evidence that improvement is possible while leaving substantial room for better methods. Its main contribution is a shared evaluation foundation and an analysis of the design choices that future work can investigate.
icml-2024-offline-multi-objective-optimi.tldr: A benchmark and methodological analysis establish a foundation for optimizing multiple conflicting objectives from fixed datasets.

paragraphs: OpenMoE provides a fully open and reproducible family of decoder-only mixture-of-experts language models. The released models range from 650 million to 34 billion parameters, with training extending beyond one trillion tokens. The study finds that mixture-of-experts models can offer a more favorable cost-effectiveness trade-off than dense language models.

A major contribution is an analysis of how tokens are routed to experts. In these models, routing depends predominantly on token identity and only weakly on surrounding context. Token-to-expert assignments also emerge early in pretraining and remain largely stable. These observations describe how specialization develops in the studied routing mechanisms.

The authors additionally find that tokens later in a sequence are more likely to be dropped. This imperfect routing can hurt performance, particularly on sequential tasks such as multi-turn conversation. They use these findings to reconsider design choices and propose possible remedies. The work combines accessible models with evidence about routing behavior, giving future designs specific issues to address without claiming that the proposed remedies are already established solutions.
icml-2024-openmoe-an-early-effort-on-ope.tldr: OpenMoE releases reproducible expert-based language models and identifies early, context-light routing and increased dropping of later tokens.

paragraphs: Probabilistic time-series models must represent uncertainty while capturing how observations relate over time. This paper addresses generative approaches whose stochastic differential equations are difficult to design and slow to sample. It introduces the decomposable denoising diffusion model, D³M, and proves that the framework unifies denoising diffusion models with continuous flow models.

Within that framework, the authors construct simple probability paths intended to speed generation. They also design a sequence-modeling module that combines a specialized state-space model with linear gated attention. This combination preserves inductive bias while representing both nearby and long-range dependencies, connecting the generation framework to the structure of time-series data.

Experiments cover eight real-world datasets. For imputation, D³M reduces RMSE by up to 4.6% and CRPS by up to 4.3% relative to state-of-the-art methods. For forecasting, it achieves comparable results with only ten steps. The findings show improved imputation performance and competitive forecasting with a short generation process, rather than uniform superiority across both tasks.
icml-2024-probabilistic-time-series-mode.tldr: D³M unifies diffusion and continuous flow modeling, improving time-series imputation and achieving competitive forecasting with ten generation steps.

paragraphs: Causal inference methods often try to reduce confounding by making treated and control groups more comparable. A central difficulty is deciding how to measure the remaining difference between their distributions. This paper defines a general balancing error for reweighted samples and uses it to study how distribution matching relates to confounding bias.

The authors connect this error to Wasserstein discrepancy, an optimal-transport measure of distribution differences. They also examine the cost function underlying that discrepancy. This matters because the cost determines how differences between samples contribute to the overall measure, so choosing a distribution distance also involves choosing which sample differences it emphasizes.

The proposed method learns both the marginal distributions and the transport cost. It implements this through joint learning of sample weights and representations associated with factual outcomes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets support the approach’s effectiveness. The contribution is a formulation that connects weighting and representation learning to the balancing error the method aims to reduce, rather than treating the discrepancy metric as an isolated choice.
icml-2024-reducing-balancing-error-for-c.tldr: A causal inference method jointly learns sample weights and representations to reduce balancing error through optimal transport.

paragraphs: Cross-domain image retrieval aims to find relevant images even when their domains differ from those encountered during training. Assembling diverse image collections for this purpose can be costly. This paper introduces a retrieval adaptation setting that uses no real training images, relying instead on an existing pretrained vision-language model.

The proposed Text-driven Knowledge Integration method first uses learnable domain word vectors to extract varied domain-specific information. It then aggregates these text descriptions to train a domain-agnostic projection containing a non-Euclidean multilayer perceptron. The training strategy expands the available domain information before learning a shared representation from it.

At test time, the learned projection is combined with the pretrained visual encoder to produce image features for retrieval. This transfer relies on the shared latent space connecting text and images. Experiments on several benchmark datasets report superior performance. The contribution is a way to adapt retrieval through textual information already accessible in a pretrained model, without requiring real images for the adaptation training.
icml-2024-retrieval-across-any-domains-v.tldr: TKI adapts cross-domain image retrieval without real training images by transferring learned text-domain structure through a pretrained vision-language model.

paragraphs: Referring expression segmentation identifies the image region described by a phrase. SemiRES learns this task from a mixture of labeled and unlabeled data. Its main target is noise in pseudo-labels, particularly around object boundaries, where inaccurate training masks can give the student model misleading supervision.

The framework uses the Segment Anything Model to improve those masks. It provides two alternative strategies, IoU-based Optimal Matching and Composite Parts Integration, for obtaining suitable masks from SAM’s candidates. When no sufficiently precise candidate can be matched, a Pixel-Wise Adjustment strategy guides student training directly through the pseudo-labels. This gives the method a way to handle both successful and unsuccessful candidate matching.

Experiments on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and G-Ref report stronger performance than fully supervised methods, especially when labeled data are scarce. With 1% labeled data, the reported gain over the supervised baseline on RefCOCO validation is 18.64%. The results support refining supervision from unlabeled examples as a useful approach to improving segmentation in low-label settings.
icml-2024-sam-as-the-guide-mastering-pse.tldr: SemiRES uses SAM-assisted pseudo-label refinement to improve referring expression segmentation when labeled data are scarce.

paragraphs: Multiagent reinforcement learning can require many interactions with an environment before agents learn effective behavior. This paper focuses on improving that sample efficiency when training uses parallel environments. Its proposed method, Multiagent Reinforcement Learning with Reset Replay, or MARR, aims to obtain more learning from the experience already collected.

MARR supports training at a high replay ratio, meaning collected experience is reused extensively for learning. To sustain that process, it introduces a reset strategy that maintains network plasticity, or the ability to keep learning. It also adds data augmentation to further improve the usefulness of the available training data.

Experiments in SMAC and MPE show that MARR improves the performance of several multiagent reinforcement learning approaches while requiring substantially fewer environment interactions. The results support the combination of repeated data use, maintained learning capacity, and augmentation in the parallel-environment setting. The contribution is an approach to making existing multiagent methods learn more efficiently from their interaction data.
icml-2024-sample-efficient-multiagent-re.tldr: MARR combines network resets and data augmentation to enable extensive replay and reduce multiagent learning’s need for environment interactions.

paragraphs: Bayesian flow networks generate data by repeatedly refining distribution parameters through Bayesian inference. Diffusion models instead refine samples. This paper connects the two approaches using stochastic differential equations, with the goal of explaining Bayesian flow networks and improving their sampling procedures for continuous and discrete data.

The authors identify linear stochastic differential equations corresponding to the noise-addition processes in Bayesian flow networks. They show that the training regression losses align with denoising score matching and interpret the original sampler as a first-order solver for the associated reverse-time equation. These connections make established diffusion sampling techniques relevant to Bayesian flow networks.

Using that connection, the authors design specialized solvers that produce better samples than the original sampler when the number of function evaluations is limited, including a ten-evaluation setting. Experiments cover image and text datasets, and the best sampler reports a five- to twenty-fold speed increase. The contribution is both a mathematical unification and a practical improvement obtained by changing how the generative process is solved.
icml-2024-unifying-bayesian-flow-network.tldr: An SDE connection between Bayesian flow networks and diffusion models enables improved samplers with reported speedups of five to twenty times.
